source_provider: Veena 2020 University of Calicut doctoral thesis
page_title: Pollination biology of selected taxa of the tribe Commelineae (Commelinaceae)
source_citation: Veena, V. (2020), doctoral thesis, Department of Botany, University of Calicut, pp. 174-176 and 181-183
source_excerpt: Breeding system studies in the selected taxa revealed that they were all self and cross-compatible species. Except Dictyospermum montanum (2.5%) and Floscopa scandens (14%), all others showed high percentages of autogamous fruit set (72.38% in Commelina diffusa, 47.62% in Murdannia nudiflora and 41.43% in Rhopalephora scaberrima). These species thus have evolved a system of adaptive modifications which resulted in a mixed mating system that produces both self and cross seeds.

source_provider: Veena 2020 University of Calicut doctoral thesis
page_title: Pollination biology of selected taxa of the tribe Commelineae (Commelinaceae)
source_citation: Veena, V. (2020), doctoral thesis, Department of Botany, University of Calicut, pp. 174-176 and 181-183
source_excerpt: Breeding system studies in the selected taxa revealed that they were all self and cross-compatible species. Except Dictyospermum montanum (2.5%) and Floscopa scandens (14%), all others showed high percentages of autogamous fruit set (72.38% in Commelina diffusa, 47.62% in Murdannia nudiflora and 41.43% in Rhopalephora scaberrima). These species thus have evolved a system of adaptive modifications which resulted in a mixed mating system that produces both self and cross seeds.
